item.title: Konosuba’s Machi-suba Is Delayed to February 2027
item.description:
Konosuba’s new game is coming later than planned. KADOKAWA announced on October 5, 2026 that Machi-suba — Kono Subarashii Sekai ni Shukufuku wo! ~Kono Aisubeki Machi ni Han’ei wo!~ — has moved from its original 2026 window to February 2027.
The announcement on the official X account says the team needs more time for development and tuning to deliver a better game, and apologises for the longer wait. Only the month has been given, not a day.
Only the date moves. Pre-registration is still open on the App Store and Google Play, and the platforms are unchanged: iOS, Android and PC, with the PC version on DMM GAMES. In September the game also named its theme song singer, Machico, who performed the opening themes of the Konosuba anime.
The new Machi-suba release date also keeps the game in Japan: no global or English version has been announced, and the store listings require a Japanese account.
The store screenshots show the two halves of the game. Between quests, players restore buildings around Axel, the starting town of the series, and raise its town rank. Out in the field, battles are fully 3D, with Kazuma, Aqua, Megumin and Darkness fighting as a party of four.
The story is new rather than a retelling of the anime. Light novel author Natsume Akatsuki supervises it, illustrator Kurone Mishima cooperates on the visuals, and the anime voice cast returns, led by Jun Fukushima as Kazuma and Sora Amamiya as Aqua.
The teaser released with the announcement in July runs through the main cast and the town, with the comedy tone of the anime intact.
It is the franchise’s first mobile game since Konosuba: Fantastic Days, which closed in both Japan and global on January 30, 2025.

item.title: Resonance Solstice Turns One With an Iron Saga Collab and a 1,500 Chaos Stone Code
item.description:
Resonance Solstice has started the first phase of its 1st anniversary with a crossover with the mecha RPG Iron Saga. The update went live on September 30 and brings Slokai, Iron Saga’s Pope of the Mechanical Vatican, as a limited SSR, a collab story event and a gift code worth 1,500 Chaos Stones.
The anniversary update was applied without downtime, and every player who logs back in receives 2 Cactus Lollipops and 1 Refresh Lollipop as compensation.
The Resonance Solstice anniversary code is FIRSTANNIV, and it gives 1,500 Chaos Stones. It works until November 8. To redeem it, tap your avatar, go to Settings, then Others, and choose Enter Redeem Code. The code is case-sensitive, so it has to be typed in capitals.
The collab event, Exodus de la Terre, runs from September 30 to October 21. It adds a collab story starring Slokai, and clearing the event stages rewards Recruit Protocols, limited avatars and UR equipment. The event’s theme is “N01R”, by Hiroyuki Sawano and Tielle.
This is the official 1st anniversary and Iron Saga collaboration PV:
Slokai is the featured SSR of the Fissure Recruit A Promised Miracle, open until October 21 at 04:59 UTC. She is voiced by Rie Kugimiya. The pity on this banner is not shared with any other Recruit.
A second banner, a Targeted Recruit running from October 1 to October 14, raises the rates of SSR Stella and SSR Nayuta. With this update, Raziel The Reminisce and Olivien also join every Recruit as regular characters.
The update also adds Joint Assault, a new event in which every player fights together against several bosses to protect the railway loop. It runs until November 5, the same day the sign-in event Commanding of the Mechanical God ends; logging in daily during it gives 10 Laplace Protocols and more.
The new brochure, Journey of Iron Saga, is available from October 1 to October 29. Unlocking it gives Slokai’s outfit “Ellie’s Afternoon”, and upgrading it adds a conductor outfit and a Slokai train livery. Completing the update are a new Calculation Recording stage, Lin, and Eliade’s outfit “Master of Arts” in the Outfit Shop.

item.title: Heaven Burns Red Japan Brings Back All Three Angel Beats! Collabs, With Up to 100 Free Pulls
item.description:
The Japanese version of Heaven Burns Red has brought back its Angel Beats! crossover in full. All three collaboration stories are playable again from October 2 at 11:00 JST until October 30 at 10:59 JST, every collab SS style returns in limited banners, and players can claim one collab SS style of their choice just for logging in.
The rerun covers every collaboration chapter released so far, all written by Jun Maeda, the creator of Angel Beats!. In Where the Cosmos Blossom, the 31-A squad wakes up underground and meets Yuri Nakamura, Kanade Tachibana and Miyuki Irie. Beautiful the Blood moves the squad to an unfamiliar school, where a cover of Crow Song wins over Hisako. The third story starts in the school cafeteria and follows Shiori Sekine as the group writes a new song with her.
The stories unlock after clearing Day 6 of Chapter 1. Each story’s exchange shop offers an S style: Miyuki Irie in the first, Hisako Fuchita in the second and Shiori Sekine in the third.
Alongside the stories, a LIVE FES. runs until October 13 with the three collab songs performed by She is Legend. This is the official live scene for Crow Song (SiL Ver.):
Every Angel Beats! SS style has been upgraded to SS and rebalanced to make it easier to use. They are split across three rerun banners:
The three banners share the same exchange points and shop, so points from any of them go to the same shop. Players looking to know which of these styles are worth the Quartz can check our Heaven Burns Red tier list.
For paying players, the Heaven Burns Red Angel Beats! rerun also brings a paid-Quartz step-up banner in which steps 3 and 6 guarantee the collab SS style of your choice, plus packs with collab ten-pull tickets on sale until October 28.

item.title: Neverness to Everness new mobile graphics was showcased for Snapdragon 8 Gen 6
item.description:
Now, Neverness to Everness is shaping up to become a showcase title for Android gaming, or more specifically, for Qualcomm’s new Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 and Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 platforms. Qualcomm is promising major advances with its latest chip generation, particularly when it comes to graphics and AI-powered rendering. NTE is one of four games Qualcomm used at Snapdragon Summit 2026 to demonstrate what the new Snapdragon hardware can achieve on mobile.
One feature already familiar from PC and consoles such as the PlayStation 5 is Unreal Engine’s Lumen lighting system. The software-based ray-traced global illumination technology will run on the new Snapdragon platform, potentially making a major difference to reflections, lighting, and the overall atmosphere of Hethereau. NTE will also support Adreno Neural Fusion (ANF), Qualcomm’s new AI-powered rendering technology. While the concept is comparable to technologies such as Nvidia’s DLSS, ANF is designed specifically for mobile hardware and combines super resolution with frame generation in a unified graphics pipeline.
The system reconstructs a full-resolution image from a lower-resolution input and can generate intermediate frames between two traditionally rendered frames. This allows compatible games to deliver higher image quality and smoother frame rates while reducing the GPU workload and power consumption. Qualcomm claims that the technology can reduce rendering power requirements by up to 40 percent, although independent testing on commercial smartphones is still limited. For a demanding open-world game like Neverness to Everness, the potential benefits are obvious: improved image quality, more stable performance, and longer play sessions before the device starts to throttle.
Qualcomm has already demonstrated Lumen and other Unreal Engine features running on its latest Snapdragon platform. The demo of Neverness to Everness on Snapdragon shows the streets of Hethereau with mobile Lumen lighting and ANF enabled:
Alongside Neverness to Everness, the games shown with Adreno Neural Fusion at the summit were Naraka: Bladepoint Mobile (NetEase), Roco Kingdom: World (Tencent) and Silver Palace (Happy Elements). Qualcomm says it is working with more than 20 partners on the technology.
If Hotta Studio can deliver on its technical ambitions, Neverness to Everness on Snapdragon could become one of the clearest demonstrations yet of what this generation of flagship Android smartphones is capable of.

item.title: Monster Hunter Outlanders Launches October 29 on iOS and Android
item.description:
Monster Hunter Outlanders launches on October 29, 2026 for iOS and Android. Capcom and developer TiMi Studio Group confirmed the Monster Hunter Outlanders release date on September 29, ahead of Tokyo Game Show 2026, and pre-registration is open now on the App Store and Google Play.
The game is a free-to-play survival hunting action title with in-app purchases, built by TiMi under license from Capcom. The mainland Chinese version is not part of this launch: it is scheduled for 2027 onwards.
Outlanders keeps the core loop of the series — track a monster, hunt it, carve materials and craft better gear — and adds exploration and Adventurers, companions gathered from different regions who fight alongside you. Crafted tools such as the Sky Glide and Wind Platforms are used to move between areas, and the game offers two control modes so it can be played comfortably on a phone.
The latest trailer, shown during an online broadcast before TGS, centres on the game’s original flagship monster, the Elder Dragon Ruger Aidal, a golden-winged dragon that fights with its sharp wings. It also shows the Adventurer Freya hunting with Buddies, the new Adventurer Haze in action, and the protagonist taking on an Azure Rathalos with a Hammer.
To mark the date, TiMi producer Dong Huang and Ryozo Tsujimoto, Capcom’s Chief Product Officer and producer of the Monster Hunter series, recorded video messages for players. The launch version adds the Charge Blade, one of the series’ signature weapons, which switches between a sword-and-shield form and a heavy axe form.
In his message, Dong Huang thanks players for their support through testing and previews the new content coming at launch and after it.
Capcom announced the date in its official press release, which frames Outlanders as its way of taking the series to a wider mobile audience.

item.title: Uma Musume Reveals Its Next Training Scenario for Late October in Japan
item.description:
Cygames has announced the next Uma Musume new training scenario for the Japanese version of Uma Musume Pretty Derby. Titled 「朋、史解き ―午式駿大祭―」, it arrives in late October 2026. Cygames revealed it on the September 27 broadcast of Pakalive TV’ #7, along with two new 3★ trainees, a story event and a new anime.
All dates below are for the Japanese version, in JST, as listed in the official announcement.
The scenario is built around the Umashiki Shundaisai, a festival that only takes place once every twelve years. Several Uma Musume are chosen for a special role in it, the sacred horses, and the festival’s shrine maiden frames it as a ritual for the bond between Uma Musume and people. It has no English title yet.
Clearing the scenario unlocks a new song, 「繚乱縁舞」 (Ryoran Enbu). A short version of its live performance is already up on the official channel:
A warm-up campaign starts in mid-October, before the scenario goes live. It hands out the Toughness 30 item and raises both the number of factor re-rolls and the number of rentals.
From September 30 at 12:00, the Pretty Derby pickup gacha adds two new 3★ trainees: [Adamant Sovereign] Symboli Rudolf and [悠久なるヘカテイア] Air Groove. The support card gacha adds two SSRs, Narita Brian and Admire Groove.
The same day, [Elegance Line] Mejiro McQueen gets Awakening Levels 6 and 7, with adjustments to her unique and inherited skills.
The next story event, Banquet of Shadows, runs from September 30 at 12:00 to October 13 at 11:59. The school festival’s main attraction this year is a food stall contest: Air Groove sets out to build the best café for Duramente, and then Symboli Rudolf enters the contest too, splitting the student council between the “Emperor” and the “Empress”. The event reward is an SSR support card of Duramente.

item.title: hololive Dreams Adds Soda Pop Lagoon, Its Third Area, and the Splash Ball Minigame
item.description:
The update also brings a new area theme song sung by the seven talents who star in the area, and a set of launch rewards worth up to 3,500 Red Diamonds.
Soda Pop Lagoon follows a new story in which players fish at different spots, collect materials and upgrade their boat. Each upgrade opens more of the sea, which leads to new locations, and the goal is to complete the area. Every fishing spot has its own fish, so there is a fish log to fill, and the catch can be traded for items at an exchange.
Seven talents lead the area and appear in its story: Houshou Marine, Yukihana Lamy, Omaru Polka, Kobo Kanaeru, Hakos Baelz, Hakui Koyori and Ichijou Ririka.
Splash Ball splits nine players into three teams of three. Each player drives a boat and pushes the ball into the other teams’ goals, and the team with the most points when time runs out wins. It is the second minigame added since launch, after Shadowbound Chase in August.
The patch also improves visibility during Lives, adds new Live options and fixes bugs.
The seven talents of the area sing PARADISE!, which joins the in-game song list with this update. Its animated music video premiered on the official hololive Dreams YouTube channel on September 28, and the song reaches music streaming services in mid-October. Our hololive Dreams song list covers every track in the game and how to unlock it.
Three campaigns celebrate the update, with dates in JST:
QualiArts and COVER had already said that new areas would arrive every few months, so Soda Pop Lagoon is the first of a planned series.

item.title: HELIOS Rising Heroes End of Service Set for December 28, 2026, with an Offline Edition to Follow
item.description:
Happy Elements has set the HELIOS Rising Heroes end of service date: the online version of the hero RPG closes at 14:59 JST on December 28, 2026, a little over six years after it launched in Japan on August 3, 2020. After that, the app will be updated into an offline edition that keeps the story and cards viewable.
The announcement, published on the game’s official site on September 28, comes with a final three-month schedule: five closing story chapters, fully voiced past events and a staged wind-down of the in-game shop.
With the main story Like the dawning light already finished, the team chose to close the game with an After Story series instead of starting a new arc. Each of the game’s sectors gets its own chapter, released in turn until November:
Every chapter comes with its own order, the game’s name for its gacha banners, and all five stay open until December 25. New events and orders stop in mid-November. In December the only additions will be character birthdays and the voicing of old events.
From December 1, past event scenarios will be fully voiced one after another, although a few events are left out.
Sales of the HELIOS PASS and Quest PASS end at 14:59 JST on October 28, and paid Ruby and packs stop selling at 14:59 JST on November 28. Players can keep spending both paid and free Ruby until the online service ends.
Paid Ruby left unused at shutdown will be refunded under Japanese law, with the procedure explained later inside the offline app. Refunds go only to bank accounts in Japan, and free Ruby or items already bought are not covered. Happy Elements asks players not to delete the app until the refund is complete.
The offline edition will show all released stories and hero cards regardless of what each player had unlocked. The planned content includes the story, the Hero Room, home customization, the album and a battle simulation. Ruby and items cannot be used there, and some stories, voice lines and music will not be included. The update date has not been announced yet.
The series continues outside the app: a sequel to the stage play Action Stage HELIOS Rising Heroes is in production, the soundtrack will be released on streaming services up to Vol. 6, and a second exhibition plus Official Visual Fanbook Vol. 3 and Official Works Vol. 2 are set for 2027.
The closure is already on our gacha end of service tracker, together with every other game shutting down this year.

The exception is Masked Hero, Avatar of Moonlight, the only older unit that still holds a place among them. Shion, the Lord of Spirits came from the “Tales of” series collaboration, the only collaboration unit in S tier.
The characters released since spring spread across the list. The four mirror-realm and abyssal units from the 4.5th anniversary, Emils, Dodomeki, Guy Crimson and Velzard, all reach the top two tiers: Velzard as an S tier protection character and the other three in A tier.
The Primordial Demons from the summer banners split in two. Testarossa, the Bewitching White Demon and Carrera, the Condemning Yellow Demon are in A tier, while Ultima, the Venomous Violet Demon sits in B. On the protection side, Esprit, the Yellow Realm Adjutant, who arrived alongside Carrera, went straight to S tier.

Ten protection characters make S tier: Esprit, the Yellow Realm Adjutant, Ramiris, the Labyrinth Berserker, Velzard, the Abyssal Frost Empress, Rimuru Tempest, Azure-Winged Fairy, Diablo, the Umbral Wolf, Veldora Tempest, the Oathbound Storm Dragon, Elmesia El Ru Thalion, the Key Sovereign, Hestia, Rimuru Tempest, the Enforcer of Justice and Shuna, the Oracle Commander.
Two of them are collaboration units: Hestia, from the DanMachi collab, and Rimuru Tempest, the Enforcer of Justice, from the “Tales of” collab.
Slime: ISEKAI Memories is Bandai Namco‘s 3D battle RPG for iOS and Android based on That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime, in which players build up the nation of Tempest and assemble troops of battle and protection characters. The 4.5th anniversary promo video shows the characters that arrived with the anniversary and the new 7★ evolution.

item.title: Sleepless Wilds Shows 18 Minutes of Gameplay as Its First Closed Test Opens in China
item.description:
Sleepless Wilds (未眠野), the open-world RPG from new studio ZEALORY Games, has released an 18-minute gameplay demo, and its first closed test is running in China from September 24 to 27. The game is coming to iOS, Android and PC, and pre-registration is open in China.
It was revealed on September 9 with a first trailer that has passed 13 million views on its official Bilibili channel. No global release has been announced yet, and ZEALORY has not detailed how the game will be monetized.
The demo follows a full day on one of the game’s island regions. Its core idea is a physics and chemistry engine in which almost everything in the world reacts to everything else: fire, metal, stone and wind can be chained together, and the game leaves players to find their own solutions. One ability lifts nearby metal into the air and sends it flying toward other metal, and smoke rising from a campfire can carry players upward for a diving attack.
Exploration covers both land and sea, with a surface world and an underground layer of strata to dig into. Players glide between islands, and the world is populated by strange, otherworldly creatures, mutated by a mysterious substance called Hazael matter.
Co-op is one of the pillars. Several players can explore and fight together, and the studio’s own pitch is that the more people there are, the more ways there are to solve a problem, whether that means lending a hand or causing chaos.
The first trailer introduces the world itself: a vast land and ocean, built on the ruins of earlier civilizations, where humanity relies on its most advanced technology to survive the changes the Hazael matter has brought.
